Every runtime claim (DPAPI, CNG persisted key and sign, Platform Crypto Provider/TPM, DACL, impersonation and client-SID check, SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION level observed, first-instance exclusivity, reject-remote) is blocked until X1 on native Windows 11 x64.

The cross-user DACL check needs a second disposable local non-admin account and the remote-client rejection needs a second Windows machine; both are listed as blocked in the run script and RESULTS.md.
The run script was only syntax-parsed by pwsh on darwin, never run.
Builds ran offline from warm caches, so network fetch and cold-cache build times were not measured. Go build time was not measured.

Only the Rust x86_64-pc-windows-gnu target (zig linker) and Go windows/amd64 were built; the MSVC target and arm64 Windows were not tried. Plain cargo build for windows-gnu fails here without mingw dlltool (the exit code was not captured).

LOC and unsafe counts are mechanical (awk/grep) and are not directly comparable across rustfmt and gofmt styles. Rust LOC includes a hand-written JSON builder, and Rust signs a fixed digest where Go hashes with sha256.
The Rust named-pipe server is blocking with no read deadlines, so a production version would need extra work not counted in LOC. The Go server uses go-winio deadlines.

go-winio behaviours (exclusive first instance via FILE_CREATE, reject-remote, DialPipeAccessImpLevel) were read from v0.6.2 source, not observed at runtime. The first Go draft's ptr() helper was replaced before the build because it would have been a stack-move hazard that go vet does not flag.
The prototypes were not edited. cargo-zigbuild was executed from prototypes/rust/target/tools/bin, read-only. Scratch outputs are under /tmp/hm-r4/M00-T05-r4-x4-windows/.
summary:
I wrote Go and Rust spikes for DPAPI, a CNG persisted P-256 key (software KSP, with a TPM Platform Provider option), a current-user-only named-pipe server with a client-SID check, and a SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION client. Both cross-compile cleanly for x86_64 Windows, but nothing has been run on Windows, so every runtime claim is blocked until X1. Go builds with CGO_ENABLED=0 on its own, while Rust needs zig plus cargo-zigbuild.

| | Go | Rust |
|---|---|---|
| Libraries | x/sys v0.46.0, go-winio v0.6.2 | windows-sys 0.61.2 only |
| cgo | not required | no C code |
| Unsafe sites | 30 | 20 |
| LOC | 504 | 698 |
| Binary | 3,279,360 B | 361,984 B |
| Warnings | 0 (`go vet`) | 0 (clippy `-D warnings`) |
| Cross-build toolchain | none | zig + cargo-zigbuild |

- **Build details:** the Rust build fails with plain cargo here because mingw dlltool is missing. Rebuilding both into a second directory gave identical SHA-256 hashes.
- **LOC and size caveats:** the Rust LOC includes a hand-written JSON builder. The size gap is not like-for-like because the profiles differ.
- **What the Go side costs:** x/sys and go-winio have no NCrypt bindings, so ten calls are hand-bound with untyped uintptr arguments. A wrong argument there compiles and only shows up at run time. Rust's windows-sys has typed signatures.
- **Rust client:** it is a std-only SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION client with no unsafe.
- **Rust server:** it is blocking with no read deadlines, which would need extra work for production. Go gets deadlines from go-winio.
- **Native runner:** `run-x4-windows.ps1` covers 15 check ids per language, including the optional TPM, cross-user DACL (needs a second local account) and remote-client checks. It was only syntax-parsed with pwsh (0 errors), not run.
